'''Thang Hoa San''' ({{langx|vi|Thang Hoa Sân}}, {{lang-zh|湯華燊}};<ref name="sbs"/> born 28 August 1954) is an Australian chemist of [[Hoa people|Chinese-Vietnamese]] background.

== Background ==
Thang was born in [[Ho Chi Minh City|Saigon]] in 1954 to Chinese parents who migrated to Vietnam in the 1930s.<ref name="sbs"/> He completed his [[Bachelor of Science]] at [[Saigon University]] in 1976, and worked as a chemist at SINCO, a sewing machine manufacturer. In 1979, Thang left Vietnam as a [[Vietnamese boat people|refugee from the Vietnam War]], and spent five months in a refugee camp in Malaysia before arriving in [[Brisbane]], Australia later in the year.<ref name="sbs">{{cite news |title=Happy Weekend with Professor San Thang |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/yourlanguage/mandarin/en/audiotrack/happy-weekend-professor-san-thang |accessdate=11 June 2018 |agency=SBS Radio |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142237/https://www.sbs.com.au/yourlanguage/mandarin/en/audiotrack/happy-weekend-professor-san-thang |url-status=dead }}</ref> He enrolled at [[Griffith University]] where he completed an Honours degree in chemistry and a PhD in organic chemistry.<ref name="csiropedia">{{cite web |title=San Thang |url=https://csiropedia.csiro.au/thang-san/ |website=CSIROpedia |publisher=CSIRO |accessdate=11 June 2018}}</ref>

In 1986, Thang joined the [[CSIRO]], the Australian government's scientific agency. In 1987, he left to join [[ICI Australia]], but returned to CSIRO in 1990.<ref name="csiropedia" /> In September 2014, research by Thomson Reuters for their [[Clarivate Citation Laureates|citation laureate prize]] named Thang as one of a trio of CSIRO scientists (together with [[Ezio Rizzardo]] and [[Graeme Moad]]) most likely to be contenders for the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] for their work in co-developing the [[reversible addition−fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization]] (RAFT) process. The three had shared the [[Australian_Academy_of_Technological_Sciences_and_Engineering#Clunies-Ross_Award|ATSE Clunies-Ross Award]] earlier that year.<ref name="trnobel">{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Bridie |title=CSIRO scientists Graeme Moad, San Thang and Ezio Rizzardo named as Nobel prize contenders |url=https://www.smh.com.au/technology/csiro-scientists-graeme-moad-san-thang-and-ezio-rizzardo-named-as-nobel-prize-contenders-20140925-10lsai.html |accessdate=11 June 2018 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=25 September 2014 |language=en}}</ref> However, in December that year, Thang revealed that he had been [[Layoff|laid off]] by the organisation in September, but had continued to work there unpaid in an honorary position.<ref name="layoff">{{cite news |title=A lesson in humility from sacked CSIRO scientist |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-12-04/csiro-scientist-sacked-from-his-job-works-for-free/5937056 |accessdate=11 June 2018 |work=ABC News |date=4 December 2014 |language=en-AU}}</ref> He later worked as a professor for [[Beijing University of Chemical Technology]], and in May 2015, joined [[Monash University]] as a professor of chemistry and was elected as a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]].<ref name="faa">{{cite web |title=Researcher elected as new Fellow to Australian Academy of Science |date=25 May 2015 |url=https://www.monash.edu/news/articles/researcher-elected-as-new-fellow-to-australian-academy-of-science |publisher=Monash University |accessdate=11 June 2018 |language=en}}</ref>
